_comment: Genuinely translucent, leaning on the compositor's blur to stay readable. Needs blur: on a compositor without it the surfaces close up automatically and you get glass-dark with extra steps. Check `glassosdctl blur` and the startup log.
_text: Pushed harder than the opaque themes. Text over a blurred backdrop competes with whatever is behind it, so the secondary tier cannot sit as low as it does on a solid card — measured at 0.70 it dropped under 4.5:1 against a light backdrop.
_surfaces: 0.78 rather than 0.72. The lower value looked better over a dark backdrop and failed badly over a bright one; blur softens detail but does not darken it.
_content: Rows stay clearly more solid than the sheet they sit on. Translucent content over translucent glass is where legibility actually falls apart.
_edge: Halved from the first attempt. At 0.34 the edge read as a drawn outline round the card rather than as light catching a pane — which is exactly the 'unseamless' look this was meant to avoid. A glass edge should be sensed, not seen.
_blur_strength: How hard the blur is is NOT set here and cannot be — ext-background-effect-v1 lets a client name the region to blur, not the radius. That is the compositor's setting: on KWin, System Settings > Desktop Effects > Blur, or kwriteconfig6 --file kwinrc --group Effect-blur --key BlurStrength <1-15>. Note a stronger blur samples a wider area, so over a bright window it pulls that brightness in and the surface goes lighter as well as hazier.
_blur: Saturation carries the material. At 1.0 a translucent surface reads as grey haze; the chroma coming through is what makes it glass rather than fog. 2.0 was too much — it tinted neutral backdrops.
_depth: Wider and softer than the opaque themes. At low alpha the fill no longer separates the surface from the desktop, so the shadow has to do that work alone.
